summary: MCV is the average size of your red blood cells. On its own it means little, but it is the fork in the road when haemoglobin is low: small cells and large cells point to entirely different causes.
what_it_measures: The average volume of a red blood cell, reported in femtolitres.

interpretations.meaning: Small red cells with a low haemoglobin point to iron deficiency or an inherited haemoglobin disorder.
typical_next_steps: haemoglobinopathy screen if ferritin is normal

interpretations.meaning: Large red cells point towards B12 or folate deficiency, alcohol, or thyroid disease.

when_to_seek_help: MCV is interpreted with haemoglobin. Discuss the pair with your GP rather than either alone.
approved_by: Demo dataset (illustrative values, not for clinical use)
